explanation.bottleneck: The source expresses transitions and outputs through full six-bit state comparisons and priority conditionals. Depending on synthesis FSM extraction and recoding, these can introduce state-decode and mux depth on setup paths. The actual critical path must be established by STA.
explanation.area_or_other_cost: Uses six state flip-flops, shared input qualification, and shallow transition logic. Explicit one-hot implementation may use more flops than a synthesis-selected compact encoding, although it avoids full-state output decoding. Mapped area must be checked against the 278.01664000000005 um2 cap.
explanation.functional_boundaries: Preserves the module name, ports, parameter declarations and defaults, single positive-edge clock, synchronous clear priority, and Moore output latency. When ten and twenty are both asserted, ten wins. DISP and RTN return to RDY on the next non-clear edge regardless of inputs. The required startup clear establishes a valid one-hot state; all transitions and arbitrary later clear assertions preserve that invariant. No additional startup or input assumptions are introduced. Illegal internal encodings before the required startup reset are not given the original default-state recovery behavior; equivalence is required over the specified post-reset behavior with default ON=1 and OFF=0.
explanation.rewrite: Implement the same six reachable states with explicit one-hot registers and direct sum-of-products transition equations. Share the ten-priority input qualifiers and derive Moore outputs directly from state bits. Retain the synchronous active-high clear on every state register.
explanation.expected_timing_gain: The rewrite is intended to reduce state-decode and transition-selection depth, especially on register-to-register paths. No timing improvement is measured or guaranteed; synthesis and STA must confirm strictly better setup WNS and non-regressing TNS at the fixed settings.
output_format_normalization: Removed complete leading think wrapper before JSON parsing
